facts.text: The hotel incorporates the Torre della Pagliazza, a tower whose origins are placed between the sixth and seventh centuries.
facts.excerpt: This is the Torre della Pagliazza, set in the intimate pocket of Piazza Sant’Elisabetta, just steps from the Duomo, yet belonging to a much earlier Florence. Its origins remain debated, but are consistently placed between the sixth and seventh centuries

facts.text: The hotel is on Piazza Sant'Elisabetta, steps from the Duomo.
facts.excerpt: set in the intimate pocket of Piazza Sant’Elisabetta, just steps from the Duomo

facts.text: The tower is widely regarded as the oldest building still standing in Florence's historic center.
facts.excerpt: it is widely regarded as the oldest building still standing in the historic center

facts.text: The tower is unusually circular and rests on Roman foundations, including a circular wall linked to a thermal structure of ancient Florentia.
facts.excerpt: it emerged that the tower rests on Roman foundations— including a circular wall linked to a basin or room of a thermal structure from ancient Florentia

facts.text: The tower was cited in 1268 as a prison and in 1285 specifically as a women's prison.
facts.excerpt: it is cited in 1268 as a prison, and in 1285 specifically as a women’s prison

facts.text: The tower was later reused as the bell tower of the nearby church of San Michele alle Trombe, later Sant'Elisabetta.
facts.excerpt: Later, the tower was reused as the bell tower of the nearby church known as San Michele alle Trombe, later Sant’Elisabetta

facts.text: Hotel Brunelleschi has a private museum where guests can see the Roman calidarium uncovered during excavations, with Roman, medieval and Renaissance artefacts.
facts.excerpt: Here, guests can discover the Roman calidarium brought to light during the excavations, together with an exceptional collection of Roman, medieval and Renaissance artefacts, historic ceramics and photographs documenting the restoration

facts.text: Two rooms are inside the tower: the Deluxe Tower Room and the Pagliazza Tower Suite.
facts.excerpt:
Two rooms. One tower. Fifteen centuries of history. Sleep inside it.

DISCOVER  THE  DELUXE TOWER  ROOM

DISCOVER  THE  PAGLIAZZA TOWER SUITE

facts.text: Rooms and suites pair contemporary Italian design with the character of the historic building.
facts.excerpt: In our rooms and suites, contemporary Italian design meets the quiet character of our historic building

facts.text: Interiors use Florentine materials such as leather and velvet.
facts.excerpt: Inside, contemporary lines meet Florentine materials: leather that softens with time, velvet that warms the light

facts.text: Some suites have views over Florence's rooftops.
facts.excerpt: Some suites open onto views that feel almost cinematic. Rooftops, stone, the quiet geometry of Florence unfolding just beyond the glass.

facts.text: The hotel offers family solutions and connecting rooms.
facts.excerpt: **Family Solutions &   Connecting Rooms**

facts.text: The Tower Bar serves cocktails inside the round stone of the ancient tower.
facts.excerpt: In the round stone of the ancient tower, the bar moves at its own tempo. Cocktails are built with precision and a sense of history

facts.text: Osteria della Pagliazza serves handmade pasta, seasonal produce and traditional Tuscan cooking.
facts.excerpt: Then comes fresh pasta, seasonal cooking and Tuscan classics at Osteria della Pagliazza

facts.text: Breakfast is served in what was once a medieval church, or can be taken in the room.
facts.excerpt: When it’s not enjoyed in pyjamas, in the quiet comfort of your room, breakfast is served in what was once a medieval church

facts.text: A restoration designed by architect Italo Gamberini (1983-1988) freed the tower and created a small archaeological display at its base, visitable on request.
facts.excerpt: designed by architect Italo Gamberini (1983–1988). The intervention freed the tower from structures that obscured it from the street and created a small archaeological display at its base, visitable on request

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler notes great views of the Duomo's dome.
facts.excerpt: There are great views of the dome; suites include your very own butler and porter; and there's an onsite gym.

facts.text: Suites include a butler and porter.
facts.excerpt: suites include your very own butler and porter

facts.text: There is an onsite gym.

facts.text: Suites feature original architectural elements such as exposed brick arches and marble.
facts.excerpt: Suites, meanwhile, are more lavish and baroque, with original architectural elements like exposed brick arches, marble, and resplendent brocades.

facts.text: Rooms have a minibar, an espresso machine and art books.
facts.excerpt: Rooms are stocked with a standard minibar and espresso machine. The art books are a nice touch.

facts.text: Condé Nast Traveler calls the concierge excellent.
facts.excerpt: The concierge is excellent.
